questions.q: What binds people together into a nation?
answer: A nation is a large body of people who feel that they belong together, even though most of them will never meet one another, which is why a nation is often called an imagined community.

answer.text: Above all, a nation is held together by a shared belief among its members that they form one community and wish to live together as one. It is not the physical features of people but this common conviction that makes a nation.

A nation usually shares a common history, with memories of struggles, achievements and heroes, and a sense of continuity from the past. It is also generally linked to a particular territory, a homeland that its people regard as their own.
Finally, a nation is united by shared political ideals and a common vision of the kind of society and state its members wish to build.

answer: Thus common beliefs, history, territory and aspirations together bind people into a nation.

questions.q: What is nationalism, and how can it be both a uniting and a dividing force?

answer.text: is the sense of belonging to a nation and the loyalty people feel towards it, and it can act in opposite ways.

list: A shared sense of nationhood can join people across region, language and religion in a common cause, as in India's freedom struggle
It can inspire sacrifice for the common good
When it stresses one language, religion or ethnicity, it can exclude and oppress minorities
It can breed hatred of other nations and lead to conflict, so nationalism must be inclusive

questions.q: How can the claims of national unity be reconciled with respect for diversity?

answer.text: like India must balance unity with the respect for its many languages, religions and cultures, and this can be done.

list: National unity need not mean uniformity; a nation can be built on shared values while celebrating diversity
Federalism and rights for minorities allow groups to keep their identity within one nation
When all groups feel respected and share equally in power and opportunity, their loyalty to the nation is strengthened
Forcing uniformity breeds resentment, whereas accommodating diversity makes unity strong and lasting
